assertions.description: Iterator.zip is a function taking one required argument (length 1).
Iterator.zipKeyed is a function taking one required argument (length 1).
With no options, iteration stops at the shortest input: zip([[1,2,3],[4]]) yields exactly one tuple.
The return value is an Iterator Helper: existing helpers like map/toArray chain directly off a zip.
A string (or any primitive) as the iterables argument throws TypeError instead of iterating characters (guarded so a browser without the static fails instead of vacuously passing).
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof Iterator === "undefined" || typeof Iterator.zip !== "function") return false; try { Iterator.zip("abc"); return false; } catch (err) { return err instanceof TypeError; } })()

assertions.description: A string element inside the iterables argument is rejected with TypeError (GetIteratorFlattenable with reject-primitives).
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof Iterator === "undefined" || typeof Iterator.zip !== "function") return false; try { Array.from(Iterator.zip(["abc", [1, 2]])); return false; } catch (err) { return err instanceof TypeError; } })()

assertions.description: A mode other than shortest/longest/strict throws TypeError (guarded).
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof Iterator === "undefined" || typeof Iterator.zip !== "function") return false; try { Iterator.zip([[1]], { mode: "weird" }); return false; } catch (err) { return err instanceof TypeError; } })()

assertions.description: Zipping zero inputs is already completed: the first next() reports done with value undefined.
assertions.test: (() => { const r = Iterator.zip([]).next(); return r.done === true && r.value === undefined; })()

assertions.description: In longest mode, exhausted inputs yield their positional padding value: zip([[1,2,3],[4]], {mode:'longest', padding:[null,0]}) yields [[1,4],[2,0],[3,0]].
options.padding is only read (Get) when mode is longest — a getter spy on options.padding must not fire in shortest mode but must fire in longest mode.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof Iterator === "undefined" || typeof Iterator.zip !== "function") return false; let shortestRead = false, longestRead = false; const s = { mode: "shortest", get padding() { shortestRead = true; return []; } }; const l = { mode: "longest", get padding() { longestRead = true; return undefined; } }; Iterator.zip([[1],[2]], s).toArray(); Iterator.zip([[1],[2]], l).toArray(); return shortestRead === false && longestRead === true; })()

assertions.description: strict mode throws TypeError mid-iteration when inputs have different lengths, after yielding the aligned prefix (guarded).
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof Iterator === "undefined" || typeof Iterator.zip !== "function") return false; const collected = []; try { for (const row of Iterator.zip([[1, 2], [3]], { mode: "strict" })) collected.push(row); return false; } catch (err) { return err instanceof TypeError && collected.length === 1; } })()

assertions.description: When the shortest input finishes, the remaining open inputs are closed: a tracked generator's finally block runs.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof Iterator === "undefined" || typeof Iterator.zip !== "function") return false; let closed = false; function* long() { try { let i = 0; while (true) yield i++; } finally { closed = true; } } const out = Iterator.zip([[1], long()]).toArray(); return out.length === 1 && closed === true; })()

assertions.description: Iterator.zipKeyed({a:[0,1],b:[2,3]}) yields records keyed like the input object: [{a:0,b:2},{a:1,b:3}].
Each record from zipKeyed is created with a null prototype (OrdinaryObjectCreate(null)).
assertions.test: (() => { const first = Iterator.zipKeyed({ a: [1] }).toArray()[0]; return Object.getPrototypeOf(first) === null; })()

assertions.description: An own enumerable property whose value is undefined is skipped entirely — its key never appears in the records.
In longest mode, zipKeyed padding is looked up by key: {mode:'longest', padding:{c:10}} pads column c with 10 and unpadded columns with undefined.
assertions.test: (() => { const rows = Iterator.zipKeyed({ a: [0, 1, 2], b: [3, 4, 5, 6], c: [7, 8, 9] }, { mode: "longest", padding: { c: 10 } }).toArray(); const last = rows[3]; return rows.length === 4 && last.a === undefined && last.b === 6 && last.c === 10; })()
